headline: K-mer and phylogenomic tools advance genome-level classification and comparison
label: Genome Comparison And Phylogenetics
summary: Recent releases and preprints extend k-mer and maximum-likelihood tools to fungal taxonomy, viral phylogenies, and bacterial genome analysis.
synthesis: The common thread is scalable sequence comparison, either by k-mer statistics or by maximum-likelihood phylogenetics, applied to whole genomes and large sequence collections. Sourmash k-mer similarity is benchmarked against ANIb and phylogenomic methods for fungal and oomycete classification from genus rank to intraspecies variants. RAxML-NG 2.0 extends maximum-likelihood inference with integrated model selection, new tree search heuristics, fast branch support metrics, and difficulty prediction. viral_usher provides a containerized tool and a monthly-updated repository of 446 viral phylogenies built from INSDC data, with a Taxonium web platform for placement. A k-mer algorithm infers alternative genetic codes more than 100-fold faster across archaeal and bacterial assemblies, and SURE-Pipe extracts shared and unique genomic regions, validated on simulated data and 96 Bacillus genomes. What is new is the use of k-mer statistics for taxonomic placement and genetic code inference, paired with continuously maintained phylogenetic resources at viral scale.
